Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

minor noun

a person under age

also minors, under age, underage, not of age, ward (of a guardian)

classical

Cic. Cat. 4.13: fīliumque ejus impūberem
Gai. Inst. 1.189: impūberēs quidem in tūtēlā esse (Lewis & Short)

impūbēs, impūberis

adjective, third declension, one ending; also impūbis, impūbe

under age, not yet grown up; as a noun, a minor

Below the age of puberty, and so in law a minor, who must have a guardian, tūtor (Gai. Inst. 1.189, Lewis & Short). The form impūbēs is Cicero’s and Caesar’s; impūbis is Horace’s, Livy’s and Tacitus’s. Of age is pūbēs.

Other words

  • minor annīs — under a given age (in law, under twenty-five)

    phrase: minor vīgintī quīnque annīs, or minor quam vīgintī quīnque annōrum · also used · post-classical · Dig. 4.4.1; Dig. 30.99.1 (Lewis & Short, s.v. parvus); M-O s.v. minor

    The lawyers’ phrase for those under twenty-five (the Digest’s title for them, 4.4: Dē minōribus vīgintī quīnque annīs); Morgan–Owens gives minor annīs, and major annīs for one of age.

  • pūpillus, pūpillī m. — an orphan; a ward under a guardian

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.1.130; Hor. Ep. 2.1.123 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. guardian: ward

    The child, fatherless, who is in a guardian’s care; feminine pūpilla.

Examples

  • fīliumque ejus impūberem lēgātum ā patre missum in carcere necātum esse dīxit

    and he said that his son, a boy under age sent by his father as an envoy, had been put to death in prisonCic. Cat. 4.13

See also minor, child, young, youth, legal.

SourcesLewis & Short: impubes · Lewis & Short: parvus · Lewis & Short: pupillus
